conclusions.reclassificationVsDisappearance: Mostly semantic relabeling for lost baseline TPs and eliminated baseline FPs; timing/coverage remain limitations across all references.
conclusions.gameplayReadiness: Evidence supports preserving non-Drop events as gameplay candidates and makes loss-of-moments less concerning for the ten lost TPs. It does not establish gameplay readiness: only 26/46 expert Drop references have any event within ±2s, mapping/playtesting are absent, and Drop preregistration still fails.
conclusions.mainIssue: For incremental baseline TP loss: semantic classification (9/10 retain moment). Across all 46 references: mixture of classification, timing (13 reference moments only at 2–5s), and event coverage (7 absent within ±5s).

recommendedDevelopmentHypothesis.text: Separate anchor-timing uncertainty from musical impact absence in grounded semantic judgments: prepared, sustained transitions with a nearby sampled rise may be conservatively demoted because the frozen anchor does not coincide exactly with an independently resolved attack. A future development study could test whether evaluating existing local temporal evidence jointly preserves true Drops while retaining resistance to ordinary re-entry overcalling.
recommendedDevelopmentHypothesis.support: Nine lost baseline TPs retained as non-Drops; all nine nearby V9 assessments cite weak/unclear impact despite sustained stronger passage; several sampled rises precede or straddle the chosen anchor.
recommendedDevelopmentHypothesis.counterevidence: Eliminated FPs frequently show the same evidence. No clean separating rule is established; no predicted improvement, new threshold, or unseen validation claim.
